approachQuestion.prompt:
Repeated beacon silence

A beacon repeats on a cycle of length P. Each silence record is (start,duration): starting at phase start, the beacon is silent for duration consecutive units while phase wraps from P back to 0. Return the total silent duration within one cycle, counting overlapping records only once. Records are unsorted and immutable. Phase intervals are half-open; silence includes its starting phase and excludes its ending phase.

Input: P=12, records=[(10,4),(1,4),(7,2)]
Output: 9
The first record covers [10,12) and [0,2). Together the first two cover [10,12) and [0,5); the third adds [7,9).

Input: P=8, records=[(3,8),(6,1)]
Output: 8
A duration equal to P covers the whole cycle.

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 1 ≤ P ≤ 1000000000; integer 0 ≤ start < P and 1 ≤ duration ≤ P. Treat time as continuous. Use comparison-based endpoint ordering rather than iterating through phases. Return one integer.

options.text: If a duration equals P, return P. Otherwise turn a nonwrapping record into [start,start+duration), and a wrapping record into [start,P) plus [0,start+duration−P). Sort the resulting pieces by start, merge their linear coverage, and sum lengths.
options.feedback: Splitting at the cycle boundary preserves exactly one cycle’s coverage. The resulting ordinary intervals can be combined without counting overlap twice; linear measure is additive even when the final covered set connects across phase zero.

options.text: Replace each record with [start,(start+duration) mod P), discard any whose end is at most its start, then merge the remaining intervals.
options.feedback: For P=12 and record (10,4), this discards the record and returns 0 instead of 4. Modulo changes the endpoint but does not represent the two pieces of wrapping coverage.

options.text: Sum every duration and cap the result at P.
options.feedback: For P=12 and records [(1,3),(1,3)], only [1,4) is silent. The answer is 3, but this method returns 6; capping cannot correct overlaps.

options.text: For each integer phase from 0 through P−1, test every record for coverage of the unit interval beginning there, and count covered units.
options.feedback: Integer endpoints make this count correct, but it enumerates the potentially billion-unit cycle and rescans all records. Boundary splitting and ordering avoid coordinate-domain brute force.

feedback.reason: Normalize wrapping coverage by splitting at the cycle boundary, preserving full-cycle and overlap semantics.
details: Scan for any full-cycle record. If absent, allocate an array with capacity 2n for normalized pieces, using a logical length, and sort those pieces by start with iterative bottom-up merge sort and a reusable buffer. Sum their union in one scan using current start/end and total; create no merged output list.

Split a wrapping silence at phase P into two linear pieces. A duration P covers the whole cycle directly. Merge normalized pieces before summing so overlap is counted once, independent of the numerical cycle length.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For split-wrap-and-measure, n is the record count. Analyze the worst case, which has no full-cycle shortcut. Count normalized pieces and sort buffer; the result is one integer. Choose the tightest standard pair.
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Count all temporary arrays and the call stack; exclude the supplied input and returned output. Numeric comparisons, assignments and arithmetic take constant time, with no overflow.
No hashing or amortized data structure is used. All loops and binary searches are iterative; there is no recursive stack.

options.text: Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(n)
Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(1)

feedback.reason: At most 2n pieces are comparison-sorted; phases themselves are never enumerated.
details: There are at most 2n linear pieces. Building and measuring them is linear; comparison sorting takes O(n log n). The normalized array and reusable buffer are O(n) auxiliary space with constant iterative scan state. A full-cycle early return improves some inputs, not this worst-case bound.
At most two pieces per record; iterative comparison merge sort; constant-time coordinate arithmetic.
“Time O(nP), auxiliary space O(P)”: The cycle phases are not enumerated. At most two pieces per record are generated, independent of P.
“Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(1)”: Normalized pieces and the reusable sorting buffer are auxiliary arrays; they do not become excluded output because the result is a scalar.
“Time O(n), auxiliary space O(n)”: A full-cycle shortcut helps some inputs, but without it the normalized pieces still require comparison sorting in the specified method.
